neet_phy_u20_t15_1.working: Silicon diodes have a knee (cut-in) voltage of about 0.7 V; germanium is about 0.3 V.

neet_phy_u20_t15_3.working: Reverse saturation current comes from thermally generated minority carriers, so it increases with temperature.

neet_phy_u20_t15_4.working: Forward current is in mA (milliammeter, IV); reverse current is in μA (microammeter, II); Ge knee voltage is about 0.3 V (III); the reciprocal of the I-V slope is dynamic resistance (I).

neet_phy_u20_t15_5.working: A is true (p side to positive terminal). B is false: the diode is non-ohmic because I is not proportional to V. C is true (reverse resistance is very high). D is true (current rises steeply past the knee). E is false (operating beyond breakdown damages an ordinary diode). So A, C and D.
